_doc: Clinic clock (TimeManager). Minutes from midnight of the business day; past 1440 is after midnight (1680 = 04:00). The clock moves with what you do: customers arriving, operations (by difficulty), talking. Periods bias who walks in (archetype weights), which incidents happen (event weights), prices, staff, lighting tint (rgba over the room), ambience (layer multipliers) and what people say. These are weights, never hard rules.

periods.label: MORNING
lines: Morning, doc. Coffee down here tastes like solder.
Before my shift. Make it quick.
You're open this early? Good.

periods.label: DAY
lines: Lunch break. I've got forty minutes.
Busy out there. Corp shuttles everywhere.
Saw a patrol two blocks up. Just so you know.

periods.label: EVENING
lines: Shift's over. Now I can afford to bleed.
Clubs open in an hour. I need to look right.
Evening, doc. Lights are coming on out there.

periods.label: NIGHT
lines: Nobody asks questions this late. That's why I'm here.
Night shift, doc? Same.
Keep the lights low. I wasn't here.

periods.label: LATE NIGHT
lines: Couldn't sleep. The chrome won't let me.
Everything else is closed, doc.
Don't look at me like that. It's three in the morning.

pacing._doc: The day's patient schedule (CustomerManager). Visits a day = the clinic's jobs a day + spare_visits (room to turn a few people away). Walk-ins on the bench use the same visits. One story case at most per day, after the first routine patient, replacing a routine visit rather than adding one. breather_sec: real seconds before the next knock after a routine patient, someone you know (returning, referral, regular) or a story case. After a story case the waiting room stays empty for quiet_minutes_after_story and no random incident follows. Random incidents are capped per day.

seasons._doc: The calendar (TimeManager.season*). Seasons follow the business day: days_per_season days each, starting with autumn on day 1. The last blend_days of a season fade into the next (light, weather, sound), so nothing changes overnight. tint: rgba laid over the hour's light (a = strength). weather: the street's precipitation (rain, sleet, snow, leaves, haze), how often a day has it and how dense it is. room: the clinic's drips (period multiplier), pipe steam and dust. ambience: layer multipliers on top of the hour's. Purely atmospheric: no prices or odds change.

autumn.label: AUTUMN
autumn.start: Storm season. The flood pumps under the Sump run all night again.
news: Storm drains overflow on Sublevel 2. Pumps 'at capacity'.
Canal level up 40 cm since Monday. Residents told to keep calm and keep upstairs.
Leaf litter from the Plaza gardens clogs the Spindle vents. Again.
lines: Storm's coming in off the bay. You can smell it in the vents.
Wet all the way down, doc. Sorry about the floor.
Pumps are loud tonight. Means the water's high.

winter.label: WINTER
winter.start: Cold front over Caldera. Sleet on the upper decks, frost on the pipes below.
news: Heating credits run out early in the Stacks. Council 'reviewing'.
Snow on Meridian Plaza for the first time in three winters. Lasted an hour.
Cold snap: chrome joint failures up 30%, say street clinics.
lines: Cold gets into the metal, doc. My arm aches where there's no arm.
Frost on the stairs. Nearly went down headfirst.
Your steam pipes are the warmest thing on the block.

spring.label: SPRING
spring.start: The thaw. Meltwater runs down every stairwell in the lower city.
news: Meltwater floods the Low Line tunnels. Trams delayed a week.
Night market moves back out under the sky.
Algae bloom turns the canal green. 'Not a health risk', says Lyra Biocomp.
lines: Everything's dripping out there. Even the light.
Thaw's started. The tunnels stink of it.
Nice to see a sky that isn't sleeting, even a brown one.

summer.label: SUMMER
summer.start: Heat over the bay. The air down here goes thick and the fans can't keep up.
news: Heat wave: cooling units sold out uptown. Again.
Rolling blackouts on Sublevel 3 'to protect the grid'.
Fever clinics report a summer spike. Officials blame the heat.
lines: Hot as a soldering iron out there.
Fans are dead on my block. Your basement's a gift.
Heat makes the chrome itch. Don't ask me why.

appointments.label: Supplier's van at the back door
